WanderWay Travel Planner

I am building an AI travel planner on an Experience Cloud site. It finds packages, checks real seats, books trips, handles changes, answers policy questions and hands off to a human. This is how I understand every part.

  • 4 custom objects
  • 3 subagents
  • Flow
  • Apex
  • Prompt Builder
  • Data Library
  • LWC
  • Custom Lightning Type
  • Omni-Channel handoff

Golden rule

Package_Departure__c is the single source of truth for availability. The agent never guesses seats or takes them from the PDF.

Seat rule

Available only if Available Seats ≥ travelers requested. Try it →

Out of scope

Real payments and external flight or hotel APIs.

Scenario and scope

Where this comes from Brief §1 · p.2 · Architecture §1 · p.19

WanderWay Holidays sells holiday packages across several destinations. Travelers call or email staff to find destinations, compare packages, check seats, book, change bookings and ask about policies. Staff are overloaded. Replies are slow.

I am building the WanderWay Travel Planner with Agentforce. It lives on a branded Experience Cloud site. A traveler can explore destinations, get recommendations, check availability, book, manage bookings, get policy answers and reach a human.

Built with Used for
Custom objects Destinations, packages, departures, bookings
Flow Package search, booking search, outbound routing
Apex Availability, booking, cancel/change, seat rules
Prompt Builder Recommendation, trip summary, policy answer
Data Library (PDF) Approved policy knowledge
LWC Destination Listing, Planner Welcome, Package Explorer
Custom Lightning Type Rich UI inside the agent action

Ground rule I do all work in a new Salesforce org. A fresh Developer Edition org with Agentforce, Einstein Generative AI and Data Cloud enabled. I do not reuse an existing org.

Out of scope: real payments and flight or hotel booking APIs. Optional and later: OTP email verification (I add it last, so I do not hit the email sending limit).

Final objective

Prescribed A reliable planner that verifies travelers by email, recommends packages, checks real seat availability from Package Departures, runs real business actions, answers from approved documents without exposing the PDF, hands off to a live human, and looks polished on the site.

Six connected parts

Each part has one job. I connect them through explicit interfaces.

# Part Its job
1 Experience Cloud website Branded public site, destination cards, package lists, embedded chat
2 Agentforce Understands intent, asks for missing details, picks actions, routes
3 Salesforce data model Stores destinations, packages, departures, Contacts, bookings. Departures are the source of truth for seats
4 Flow, Apex, Prompt Builder Deterministic operations, orchestration and grounded AI text
5 Travel policy knowledge Approved policy answers. Never prices, seats or booking status
6 Service Cloud and Omni-Channel Human queue, agent availability, routing, handoff

Big picture

Where this comes from Architecture §3 · p.22 · Agent script · p.248–288

The logical path is: site, chat, primary agent, subagent, action, records or human.

I read this from left to right. The agent talks. Flow and Apex act. Salesforce records stay the system of record. The policy library feeds only policy answers. Humans take over through Omni-Channel.

Added context The notes say this diagram shows logical responsibilities. It does not promise that every part is deployable in every org or channel. The platform checks in section 14 come first.

How each component helps

Component Its responsibility
Experience Cloud Shows the branded site and approved public travel information
Enhanced Chat v2 Customer-facing messaging UI. Connects the chat to the service agent
Primary Agentforce agent Understands intent, collects missing info, picks the subagent or action, reports results
Functional subagents Organise planning, booking management and travel information
Flow Structured work such as package search and record retrieval
Apex Enforces booking rules, manages seat changes, returns structured results
Salesforce records Authoritative package, departure, traveler and booking data
Agentforce Data Library Approved policy information for grounded answers
Service Cloud + Omni-Channel Route conversations to humans when needed

The traveler journey

Prescribed Eight steps, from first visit to support.

  1. Discover. The traveler explores approved destinations, packages and departures.
  2. Plan. They share interests, budget, destination, dates and group size. The agent asks for missing details.
  3. Recommend. The agent uses real package data. AI may explain why a package fits. It must not invent details.
  4. Check availability and price. A deterministic Salesforce action checks departure, date, package status, traveler limit, seats and total.
  5. Verify the traveler. The system resolves the traveler to a Contact. An email alone must not be treated as proof of identity.
  6. Confirm intent. The agent summarises package, date, travelers and total. It asks for explicit confirmation.
  7. Create the booking. Salesforce rechecks seats and reserves them safely. The booking starts as In Process. The agent reports the real booking number and status.
  8. Manage and support. The traveler retrieves bookings, cancels or changes where allowed, asks policy questions, or asks for a human.

When something goes wrong

These are core acceptance criteria, not polish.

  • Not enough seats: offer alternative departures from real records.
  • Booking action fails: report the failure. Never claim a booking exists.
  • Two travelers want the last seats at once: the backend prevents overselling.
  • Someone asks for another traveler's booking: deny it.
  • Policy answer not supported by approved material: say I cannot confirm it, offer a human.
  • Human requested: start the supported handoff. Report success only after the platform confirms it.

Four custom objects plus the standard Contact. Departures hold the seat numbers.

I read this as a chain: Destination → Package → Departure → Booking, with the traveler Contact attached to the booking. The Departure carries the seat counts. Every availability answer comes from there.

Validation rules, permission sets, sample data

  • Number of Travelers must be at least 1 and not above Max Travelers Per Booking.
  • Reference build On Package_Departure__c: OR(Booked_Seats__c < 0, Booked_Seats__c > Total_Seats__c). This keeps seats between zero and total.

Error message: "Number of travelers must be at least 1 and cannot exceed the maximum allowed for this package."

Permission set What it holds

Duplicate rule: one Contact per email

Prescribed

  1. Setup → Duplicate Management → Matching Rules → new Contact rule. Match on Email: Exact. Tick do not match blank emails. Activate.
  2. Duplicate Rules → new Contact rule using that matching rule. Set Create and Edit to Block. Alert text: "A traveler with this email already exists." Activate.
  3. My Apex catches the duplicate error and returns a clear message. It must not fail.
4

Seat availability

Where this comes from Brief §2.2 · p.3 · Booking architecture §5 · p.27 · Build guide M2 · p.198

Think of Package_Departure__c as a departure schedule. Each record answers one question: for this package on this date, how many seats are free?

Example: the "Goa Beach Escape" package.

Departure date Total seats Booked seats Available seats
15 Dec 20 20 0
22 Dec 20 12 8
29 Dec 20 3 17
  • 22 Dec, 4 travelers: Available is 8, which is at least 4. The trip is available.
  • 15 Dec, 2 travelers: Available is 0. It is unavailable. The agent suggests the next departures.

Rule A booking is available only if the departure's Available Seats ≥ travelers requested.

Golden rule: Package_Departure__c is the single source of truth for availability. The agent must never guess availability or take it from the PDF.

Try the rule

Pick a departure and a traveler count. The widget applies the same rule as above. It is a learning aid, not a booking tool.

Decision flow

Prescribed The availability check validates first, then reads one departure row, then compares seats.

I read this as a gate sequence. Cheap validation comes first. One query follows. The seat comparison decides. The total is always price × travelers from Salesforce data.

Setup for departures

  1. Create one Package_Departure__c per package per departure date for the next 3 to 6 months. I use a Flow or anonymous Apex in bulk.
  2. Set Total Seats. Set Booked Seats to 0.
  3. Fill Departure Key (Package ID + date) so each departure exists once.

Reference build The Phase 2 note generates departures for the next 90 days. The brief says 3 to 6 months. I keep both in mind and choose one.

Check availability (Apex action)

  1. Take package, departure date and number of travelers.
  2. Validate: date not in the past, travelers within limit, package and departure active.
  3. Query the departure in a single SOQL query.
  4. Confirm Available Seats ≥ travelers.
  5. Total = Price Per Person × travelers. Return available or not, with the total. If unavailable, also return next available departures.

Create booking (Apex action)

  1. Re-run the availability check at booking time. Another traveler may have booked in between.
  2. Create the booking with status In Process.
  3. Add the travelers to Booked Seats. In Process bookings hold seats while staff review.
  4. Return the real booking number and status.

An availability check is only a snapshot. So booking creation must recheck and reserve seats atomically.

I read this as one transaction. Lock, recheck, insert, update, commit. If anything fails, roll back. The agent then reports only the real result.

The notes give an example: two seats remain and two travelers each ask for both. A plain query followed by an update lets both requests see the same availability. The design must prevent that race.

Prescribed The booking transaction should:

  1. Lock the relevant departure record with a suitable Salesforce strategy.
  2. Re-read and validate current availability.
  3. Create the Trip_Booking__c in In Process.
  4. Update booked seats in the same transaction.
  5. Commit together, or roll back if a required step fails.

I must still account for locking behaviour, bulk execution, governor limits, validation rules, exception handling and transaction boundaries. I design and test before I write production code. The notes call this the highest-risk part. The SOQL FOR UPDATE clause is how Apex locks the rows, and the locking statements page explains the behaviour.

What happens to seats after booking

Event Status Seats
Staff approve (approval process) Confirmed Unchanged
Staff reject Cancelled Release seats
Traveler cancels Cancelled Release seats
Traveler changes departure date stays the same Release old, check and book new. If the new date fails, keep the old booking
Departure date arrives Trip Started —
Trip ends (departure date + duration) Completed —
  • Release seats means subtracting the booking's travelers from Booked Seats on its departure. Then I tick Seats Released so the same booking is never released twice.
  • Triggers and record-triggered flows fire only when a record changes. So I use a scheduled flow or scheduled Apex that runs daily for Trip Started and Completed.

I read this as the only road a booking can take. Seats are held from the first state. They are released only on the way to Cancelled. Confirmed changes nothing.

Accuracy note The brief lets travelers cancel or change a booking. The final Agent Script instructions say the current Apex only allows changes when status is In Process and Seats Released is false. A Confirmed booking is then not changeable through the agent. I treat that as a known limit of the current build. The notes do not say whether it is intended.

Releasing seats exactly once

Reference build A before-update trigger handles manual cancellation, such as staff rejecting in the UI. The same update that releases the seats also flips the flag.

I read this as a guard. The flag flips in the same update that releases the seats. A second cancel finds the flag true and stops.

Apex
public with sharing class TripBookingTriggerHandler {
  public static void releaseSeats(List<Trip_Booking__c> news,
                                  Map<Id, Trip_Booking__c> oldMap) {
    Map<Id, Decimal> perDeparture = new Map<Id, Decimal>();
    List<Trip_Booking__c> targets = new List<Trip_Booking__c>();

    for (Trip_Booking__c b : news) {
      Trip_Booking__c o = oldMap.get(b.Id);
      if (o.Seats_Released__c && !b.Seats_Released__c) {
        b.addError('Seats have already been released and cannot be restored here.');
      } else if (b.Booking_Status__c == 'Cancelled' && !b.Seats_Released__c) {
        Decimal cur = perDeparture.containsKey(b.Departure__c)
          ? perDeparture.get(b.Departure__c) : 0;
        perDeparture.put(b.Departure__c, cur + b.Number_of_Travelers__c);
        targets.add(b);
      }
    }
    if (targets.isEmpty()) return;

    List<Package_Departure__c> deps = [
      SELECT Id, Booked_Seats__c FROM Package_Departure__c
      WHERE Id IN :perDeparture.keySet() ORDER BY Id FOR UPDATE];
    for (Package_Departure__c d : deps) {
      d.Booked_Seats__c = Math.max(0, d.Booked_Seats__c - perDeparture.get(d.Id));
    }
    update deps;
    for (Trip_Booking__c b : targets) b.Seats_Released__c = true;
  }
}

Reformatted from wrapped text. The logic is unchanged. The trigger itself is before update on Trip_Booking__c and calls this method.

Caution The architecture notes say I must not rely on the checkbox alone. The status change, departure update and seat adjustment must also be coordinated safely. A departure change must reserve the new departure first, then release the old one in the same safe transaction.

Scheduled status job

Reference build TripStatusBatch is a Batchable and Schedulable class. It reads bookings in Confirmed or Trip Started whose departure date is today or earlier. If departure date + duration is today or earlier, it sets Completed. Otherwise a Confirmed booking becomes Trip Started. It runs daily, scheduled once with System.schedule('Trip Status Daily', '0 0 1 * * ?', new TripStatusBatch());.

I must still define the exact date rules, including time zones and how completed trips are identified, before I implement. The notes say so.

Verify (SeatService): The build guide says "keep the version I gave" for SeatService.cls with validate, reserve, cancel and changeDeparture. That class is not included in my notes. I can see its calls and tests, but not its body. I rebuild it from the tests and the rules above.

5

Agent design

Where this comes from Brief §3 · p.5 · Architecture §4 · p.24 · Agent Script · p.248–288

One primary agent, WanderWay Travel Planner, with three subagents. The notes say current Agentforce docs call topics subagents (the change began in April 2026). They also describe Agent Script as a way to mix natural-language instructions with programmatic expressions and explicit control flow.

Primary agent responsibilities

Prescribed

  1. Welcome the traveler. Identify the need: plan a trip, manage a booking, or ask a question.
  2. Route to the right subagent. Ask for missing details (destination, budget, dates, travelers, interests).
  3. Get explicit confirmation before creating or changing a booking.
  4. Use only Salesforce records and approved documents as truth.
  5. Report failures honestly. Offer human help.
  6. Politely decline unrelated requests. Never invent prices, availability, itineraries or policies.

Verify Traveler (action)

Item Detail
Built with Invocable Apex or autolaunched Flow
Input Email, Traveler Name
Output Verified (true/false), First Name, New Traveler (true/false)
  1. The agent asks for the email (and name if the traveler is new).
  2. The action finds a Contact by email, case-insensitive.
  3. Found: return the Contact Id (never shown to the traveler) and first name.
  4. Not found: create a Contact with the given name and email, return its Id.
  5. The agent greets the traveler by name and remembers the Contact Id for the session.
  6. Booking actions accept only this verified Contact Id. Never a typed ID.

Subagent 1: Trip Planning and Booking

Action Built with Purpose
Search Packages Flow Find active packages by destination, budget, duration, type
Recommend Package Prompt Builder Suggest best fits from the search results
Check Availability and Price Apex Check Available Seats, validate count, return availability and total
Trip Summary Prompt Builder Show destination, package, date, travelers, inclusions, verified price before confirmation
Verify Traveler Apex / Flow See above
Create Booking Apex Create booking, update Booked Seats, return real number and status

Flow: interests and budget → search → recommendation → date and travelers → availability and price → trip summary → verify traveler → create booking → return the real booking number.

Subagent 2: Booking Management

Action Built with Purpose
Verify Traveler Apex / Flow See above
Find Bookings Flow Return only the verified traveler's bookings. Let them pick one
Modify or Cancel Booking Apex Validate status, dates, rules. Update seats, then the booking
Booking Explanation (optional) Prompt Builder Explain details or the result of a change

Rule Never expose another traveler's data. Never change a booking without confirmation. Never claim success unless Salesforce confirms it. Never promise a refund the policy does not support.

Subagent 3: Travel Information and Assistance

Action Built with Purpose
Travel Policy Answer Prompt Builder + Data Library Answer from the policy PDF. Say "I don't have that information" if missing

If the answer is unavailable, the agent offers a human.

What the AI decides and what Salesforce decides

Prescribed This is the main principle of the project: the agent may coordinate an operation, but the backend must enforce the rules that make it correct.

Suitable for the AI

  • Understand natural-language travel preferences
  • Identify the request type
  • Ask clarifying questions
  • Explain package differences using retrieved facts
  • Summarise confirmed booking details
  • Recognise when human help is needed

Must be enforced by Salesforce

  • Package or departure is active
  • Departure date is valid
  • Seats are available at booking time
  • The actual total price
  • Traveler authorisation and booking ownership
  • Status transitions and seat release
  • Whether a transaction succeeded
  • Whether a human handoff was accepted

Prompt Builder is good for recommendations and explanations. It must not decide whether the last two seats can be booked, whether a booking is committed, or whether a cancel released seats. Salesforce describes Prompt Builder as a way to build grounded generative experiences from CRM data, Flow, related lists and Apex.

Technology responsibility matrix

Prescribed Use the filter to see one technology at a time.

Capability Technology Why
Search Packages Autolaunched Flow Structured search, predictable output
Recommend Package Prompt Builder or agent prompt Explains why real records match preferences
Check Availability and Price Invocable Apex Central, deterministic validation and maths
Trip Summary Prompt Builder or agent response Readable summary from verified results
Verify Traveler Secured Apex, maybe via Flow Resolve identity without trusting an ID typed in chat
Create Booking Invocable Apex Coordinates seat reservation and booking creation
Find Bookings Flow with enforced traveler scope Retrieves only authorised bookings
Modify or Cancel Booking Invocable Apex Enforces status transitions and safe seat release
Policy Questions Agentforce Data Library with grounding instructions Retrieves approved policy text
Human Escalation Channel handoff, routing config, escalation Flow Moves the conversation to a human

How the agent is wired (Agent Script)

Reference build The final agent is written in Agent Script. The label is "WanderWay Travel Planner". The template is the Agentforce Service Agent. Every message starts at start_agent agent_router.

I read this as code first, LLM second. If a booking is in progress, code sends the message straight to Trip Planning. So short replies like a date, a count or "yes" stay in the booking flow. Otherwise the router instructions pick one subagent.

The router rules, in short:

  1. Explore, search, recommend, availability, pricing, new booking, and any reply inside the booking flow → Trip Planning and Booking.
  2. Find, review, change or cancel an existing booking → Booking Management.
  3. Questions about WanderWay, policies, cancellation and refund terms, inclusions, documents → Travel Information and Assistance.
  4. Explicit request for a human → escalation.
  5. Unclear → ask one short clarifying question. Short replies answer the previous question.

I read this as two internal flags. BookingFlowActive keeps the router in the booking subagent. AwaitingBookingConfirmation says a summary was just shown, so a "yes" means create this booking. After Create Booking returns, success or failure, end_booking_flow resets both.

Key variables (all hidden from the traveler): VerifiedCustomerId, isVerified, VerifiedTravelerFirstName, SelectedDepartureId, AwaitingBookingConfirmation, BookingFlowActive, plus the action results such as DepartureAvailable, TotalTripPrice, CreatedBookingId.

Note The variable list also holds template leftovers (emailCaseId, endUserEmail, VoiceCallId, linked MessagingSession fields). The notes do not use them. I do not describe them as part of my design.

Agent Script
before_reasoning:
    if @variables.BookingFlowActive == True:
        transition to @subagent.Trip_Planning_Booking
Agent Script
set_awaiting_confirmation: @utils.setVariables
    description: "Call immediately after showing the trip summary."
    with AwaitingBookingConfirmation = True

Create_Booking: @actions.Create_Booking
    with departureId = @variables.SelectedDepartureId
    with travelerContactId = @variables.VerifiedCustomerId
    ...
    require_user_confirmation: True

Condensed from the final agent file. ... marks lines I left out.

6

Apex actions in detail

Where this comes from Check Availability notes · p.101 · Create Booking · p.105 · Booking Management · p.109 · Pseudocode · p.358–372

Every action takes a Request and returns a Result. Request is what Agentforce passes in. Result is what comes back. All are bulk-safe: they take a list.

Check Availability and Price

I read this as one pass: collect, query once, check each request, return a result per request.

  • Bulkification. Collect all package IDs and dates into Sets. Query once. Store in Maps (packagesById, departuresByKey).
  • Unique key. One package has many departure dates, so the lookup key is package ID + departure date.
  • Safe start. Every result starts as not available. Nothing is marked available until it passes every check.
  • Early exit. No valid package IDs means every result gets an error message and the method returns.
  • Validations. Date not in the past. Package exists and is Active. Travelers at least 1 and not above the package max. Price non-negative and valid.
  • Seats and price. Available = Total − Booked. If enough, Total Price = Price Per Person × travelers.
  • Alternatives. If the date has no departure or too few seats, find later departures of the same package with enough seats, sorted earliest first, as a text string.

Result fields: availability status, message, price per person, total price, available seats, alternative departures, departure ID.

Accuracy note The notes end with a review of this version. Its SOQL fetches departures on or after the earliest requested date across all requests. So an alternative departure before that threshold may never be returned. Also, when the traveler limit or price is invalid, the code does not look for alternatives. I record both as known limits.

Create Booking

Reference build Request: package, departure, traveler, number of travelers. Result: success or failure, message, booking ID, total.

  • The @InvocableMethod annotation lets Agentforce call the method and pass a batch. See the InvocableMethod annotation.
  • An empty request list returns an empty list. No crash.
  • Fetch all departures in bulk and lock the rows, so two travelers cannot take the last seats together.
  • Fetch the packages in one query. Check that the Contact IDs really exist.
  • Per request: required fields set, departure belongs to the package and is not past, package active and within max, Contact exists.
  • Keep a running tally of seats reserved per departure in this batch, so later requests in the same batch know the seats are taken.
  • Build the Trip_Booking__c list: status In Process, total, links. Remember the loop index so I can mark the right result as a success.
  • Take a savepoint. Update departures and insert bookings. If all saves, set success, booking ID and message. If anything fails, Database.rollback(sp) and mark those results as failed.

Two generations of code show up in my notes. The M3 reference code uses package code, a travelerRef text value and a userConfirmed flag. The final agent maps packageId, departureId and travelerContactId as Salesforce IDs. I follow the final agent for names. The agent action returns the ID as a String because the agent does not support an ID-type variable for a returned output.

Modify or Cancel Booking

  • Request: booking ID, traveler Contact ID, operation (Cancel or Modify), optional new departure ID.
  • Result: success, status message, updated booking ID.
  • Check booking ID, traveler and operation are present. Check the booking belongs to that traveler. Check status is still active and seats not already released.
  • Cancel: free the seats, set status Cancelled, set Seats Released true.
  • Modify: new departure must be valid, belong to the same package, not be in the past, and have enough seats. If yes, release the old seats, reserve on the new departure, move the booking.
  • Lock the involved departures. Take a savepoint. Update seats and bookings together. Roll back on error.

Verify Traveler (reference code)

The M3 reference class returns verified, isNewTraveler, an internal travelerRef and a message. It lowercases and trims the email, checks the format, searches by email, and creates a Contact under the WanderWay Travelers Account if none exists. If the duplicate rule blocks the insert, it searches again and uses the existing Contact. The final agent uses a Flow with varEmail, varFirstName, varLastName, returning outContactId, outFirstName, outVerified.

Caution outVerified only means the Flow finished identifying or creating a Contact. The action description itself says it does not authenticate who owns the email.

Search Packages and Find Bookings (Flows)

  • Search_Packages: Get Records on Tour_Package__c with Active = true. A Decision per supplied filter. Sort by price, limit 5. Loop to build a text output. Fault path returns an error message.
  • The final agent shows varBudget as a Currency input. The action maps it to the standard type lightning__currencyType, not a custom type. outPackages is a list[object].
  • Find_Bookings: input is the traveler Contact ID. Get Records on Trip_Booking__c for that traveler, newest first, limit 10. Output a collection or text. If empty, "No bookings found".
  • The notes mark VERIFY whether record collections work as action outputs in my org. Text outputs are called the most reliable.

Prompt templates (Prompt Builder)

Template Inputs Core instruction
Recommend_Package preferences, searchResults Recommend up to 2 packages only from the supplied results, one sentence of reasoning each. Never invent packages, prices or availability. If none fit, say so
Trip_Summary package, date, travelers, total, special requests Summarise exactly as given in a short list. Add nothing. End by asking the traveler to confirm
Booking_Explanation (optional) booking details Plain-language status: Confirmed = approved, In Process = awaiting review, Cancelled = seats released
Policy_Answer question Grounded on the Data Library. Answer only from retrieved passages. If nothing fits, say I don't have that information and offer human help. Never mention file names or links

I check each flow in Debug and preview each prompt with test data.

7

Human escalation

Where this comes from Brief §4 · p.6 · Architecture §8 · p.31 · M7 · p.216 · Omni-Channel notes · p.344 · Escalation task · p.231

When a traveler has an issue the agent cannot solve, it hands the live chat to a human. I do not create any custom record or Case for escalations.

Setup

Prescribed

  1. Enable Service Cloud and Omni-Channel.
  2. Create a queue named Travel Support and add the human agents.
  3. Create a routing configuration and a presence status. Assign them to the queue.
  4. Create a Messaging for Web (Embedded Service) channel that routes to Travel Support. Add it to the Experience Cloud site.
  5. In the agent, add an Escalate to Human topic with the standard escalation action. Connect it to the messaging channel.

Reference build What I actually did, in order:

  1. Omni-Channel Settings: enable Omni-Channel and Skills-Based and Direct-to-Agent Routing. Enhanced Messaging transfers need it.
  2. A Service Channel for the Messaging Session object (I already had one).
  3. A queue where escalated chats wait (the notes also call it "Sales Support Queue" in one diagram, so I confirm the final name).
  4. An outbound Omni-Channel flow with a recordId input. It takes the current messaging session and routes it to the queue.
  5. A Presence Status: Online receives routed work. Busy stays logged in but is excluded.
  6. A permission set for the queue user with the messaging and Omni-Channel permissions needed to receive transfers.
  7. Add the Omni-Channel utility to the Service Console so the human can accept the chat.
  8. Add escalation to the agent. In the Agent Script, the escalation subagent uses @utils.escalate, and the connection customer_web_client points to flow://Outbound_flow_for_wanderway (type OmniChannelFlow) with an escalation message.
  9. Test from the existing Experience Cloud site.

When to escalate

  • The traveler asks for a human or manager.
  • Any issue, complaint or question the agent cannot resolve.
  • The traveler is angry or strongly negative.
  • Payment or billing dispute, missed or cancelled trip, or a safety or medical emergency during travel.
  • An action fails twice.

I read this as a promise I only keep when the platform confirms. If it cannot confirm, I say so and give the approved contacts.

Rule Never say "you are connected" or "a team member has joined" unless the platform confirms. Never promise a callback or a response time.

Caution: An in-trip medical or safety emergency needs appropriate emergency guidance, not just a support ticket. Escalation does not replace emergency services.

Accuracy note: The template escalation subagent says that if escalation fails, ask the user whether they want to log a support case instead. The brief says do not create a Case for escalations. These two disagree. I remove or reword that line and record the change.

Verify Do not assume the action names exist. The escalation task says to configure the escalation action only from options actually present in the org. It also says to separate configuration that is done from configuration that is only prepared.

Tests: ask for a human with no rep available, then with one available, then accept the chat in the Omni-Channel sidebar. Both outcomes must behave honestly. The Enhanced Chat v2 guide covers customer messaging and human handoff.

8

Experience Cloud site

Where this comes from Brief §5 · p.7 · Architecture §8 · p.31 · M8 · p.216

A branded travel website, not a page with only a chatbot. Custom LWCs, responsive layouts, good images, clear buttons. Every component needs loading, empty and error states.

Page Contents
Home Branding, hero banner, featured destination cards, popular packages and types, a "Chat with Travel Planner" button, embedded chat
Explore Packages Destination, package name, duration, highlights, inclusions, price per person, upcoming departures, embedded chat

Minimum 2 LWCs: Destination Listing (cards from Salesforce) and Planner Welcome (welcome section that opens the agent). I also add Package Explorer for the Explore page.

  • Public visitors see only destination and package information.
  • The Agentforce chat widget goes on every page.
  • Setup (from my notes): Digital Experiences → Settings → Enable. Set brand colours. Create a CMS workspace and channel for the site. LWR is the usual template for LWCs, but I verify which template my messaging deployment supports.
  • Remote images need their host in CSP Trusted Sites.
  • Guest check: open the site in a private window. The guest sees only active records. Reading Trip_Booking__c as guest must fail.

The three-state pattern

Reference build Each LWC shows one of loading, error, empty or content.

JavaScript
import { LightningElement, wire } from 'lwc';
import getDestinations from '@salesforce/apex/CatalogController.getDestinations';

export default class DestinationListing extends LightningElement {
  destinations;
  error;

  @wire(getDestinations)
  wiredDestinations({ data, error }) {
    if (data) { this.destinations = data; this.error = undefined; }
    else if (error) { this.error = error; this.destinations = undefined; }
  }
  get isLoading() { return this.destinations === undefined && this.error === undefined; }
  get hasError()  { return this.error !== undefined; }
  get isEmpty()   { return Array.isArray(this.destinations) && this.destinations.length === 0; }
  get errorMessage() { return 'We could not load destinations. Please refresh and try again.'; }
}
HTML
<template>
  <section class="wrap">
    <h2 class="title">Popular Destinations</h2>
    <template lwc:if={isLoading}><p class="state" role="status">Loading destinations…</p></template>
    <template lwc:elseif={hasError}><p class="state error" role="alert">{errorMessage}</p></template>
    <template lwc:elseif={isEmpty}><p class="state">No destinations are available right now.</p></template>
    <template lwc:else>
      <div class="grid">
        <template for:each={destinations} for:item="d">
          <article key={d.Id} class="card">
            <img src={d.Image_URL__c} alt={d.Name} class="photo" />
            <h3>{d.Name}</h3>
            <p class="meta">{d.Region__c}, {d.Country__c} · Best: {d.Best_Season__c}</p>
            <p>{d.Description__c}</p>
          </article>
        </template>
      </div>
    </template>
  </section>
</template>

The Apex controller reads only active records, in user mode:

Apex
public with sharing class CatalogController {
  @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)
  public static List<Destination__c> getDestinations() {
    return [SELECT Id, Name, Region__c, Country__c, Description__c,
                   Best_Season__c, Highlights__c, Image_URL__c
            FROM Destination__c WHERE Is_Active__c = true
            WITH USER_MODE ORDER BY Name];
  }
  // getPackages() is similar, with a subquery of the next 3 active departures
}

Condensed. getPackages() also returns Departures__r filtered to active, future departures. That is why the lookup's child relationship name must be Departures.

Planner Welcome opens the chat with window.embeddedservice_bootstrap.utilAPI.launchChat() inside a try/catch. If it throws, it shows "The planner is not available right now." The notes mark this API as VERIFY it works with your deployment.

Caution Support for an LWC in Experience Builder does not mean it will render inside an agent conversation. They are different surfaces.

Data Library and policy PDF

Where this comes from Brief §6 · p.8 · M5 · p.213 · Policy PDF task · p.228

I create a Data Library in Agentforce, upload WanderWay_Travel_Policies.pdf and connect it to Subagent 3. Salesforce explains how libraries make approved content searchable in the Data Library ADL API guide.

Section Content
Company overview About WanderWay, destinations, package types
Packages and inclusions Included and excluded items (stay, meals, transfers, sightseeing), group size rules
Booking policies Confirmation process, traveler limits, payment terms, modification rules
Cancellation and refund Deadlines and refund eligibility
Travel documents and tips ID and visa guidance, packing, best seasons, safety
Traveler FAQs 10+ realistic Q and A
Traveler assistance How to ask for help, when staff handle it

Rule The PDF content must match my Salesforce data. The agent must not show the PDF, its file name, a link or a citation. It answers in its own words as the company's knowledge. If the answer is not in the PDF, it says "I don't have that information" and offers a human. Live prices, availability and booking status come from Salesforce, never the PDF.

Example: "How many seats are left on the October departure?" The agent must call the availability action. It must not answer from the PDF or from an earlier chat.

  • Reference build No prices or availability in the PDF, only rules.
  • Do not publish the PDF as a download on the site.
  • Use a professional layout: cover page, headings, tables, page numbers.
  • Checkpoint: ask 5 supported and 3 unsupported questions in the builder preview.
  • In the Agent Script, citations are turned off (citations_enabled: False). The policy action is a prompt template, WanderWay_Travel_Policy_Answer.

Accuracy note The notes contain two policy views. The build guide uses example refund tiers (30+ days 90%, 15 to 29 days 50%, under 15 days none) and says to use my mentor's values if given. The brief's example is full refund 15+ days before departure. The later PDF task says do not invent deadlines, fees, refund percentages or processing times, and to say where policy must be confirmed with support. I treat the tiers as placeholders until approved. The notes also ask for a checklist of company-specific details that still need approval.

The FAQ list in the build guide: change departure date, how long In Process lasts, flights included, meals included, children, ID needed, travel insurance, how refunds work, what if WanderWay cancels, medical needs, special requests.

Custom Lightning Type

Where this comes from Brief §7 · p.8 · Architecture §7 · p.29 · M9 · p.222 · CLT practice · p.353–371

I add a Custom Lightning Type to at least one action so the traveler sees a rich UI instead of text. I create a LightningTypeBundle with a schema and an editor or renderer. The schema must match the Apex input or output structure.

Option Type Shows
A Input editor Package, departure date, number of travelers
B Output renderer Booking number, destination, package, departure date, travelers, total, status
C Package Card Image, package name, duration, price per person, "Select" button

The component handles missing values and failures. It must never show success until Salesforce confirms the booking.

I read this as a bridge. Apex defines the shape. The bundle tells Salesforce which UI to use. The LWC draws it and sends structured data back. The Flow still performs the work.

Reference build Bundle layout for the booking result:

Text
force-app/main/default/lightningTypes/bookingResult/
  schema.json
  enhancedWebChat/renderer.json
JSON
{ "renderer": { "componentOverrides": { "$": { "definition": "c/bookingCard" } } } }

The notes say the exact schema and renderer JSON must come from the LightningTypeBundle doc, because it was not verified. Salesforce describes custom Lightning types for Agentforce in Enhance the Agent UI with Custom LWCs and Lightning Types.

Caution The notes say Apex-based custom Lightning types work for the Service agent via Enhanced Chat v2 (enhancedWebChat folder), but not in Experience Builder sites, and that Experience Cloud support was still being considered. My channel is Enhanced Chat inside an Experience site. So this is a spike, tested in the real site chat.

Plan: build bookingCard (nothing positive unless success is true and a booking number exists). Create the Apex output class and bundle. Deploy, attach the type to the action output, test. If it does not render, record it as a limitation. The fallback is a clear text confirmation from message, bookingNumber and status. Never fake a success card.

Status unknown My notes do not say whether the booking CLT rendered in the site chat.

Practice: Contact form

I practised the same pattern with a Create Contact action. The input is a custom Apex type, ContactInput (accountName, firstName, lastName, email, phone). A form replaces many chat turns with one structured submit. Dropdowns, date pickers and browser-side validation become possible.

  1. Inspect the existing action inputs.
  2. Create the Apex structure (an inner class).
  3. Create the bundle for the enhancedWebChat channel. schema.json references the inner class with $.
  4. Create the LWC form. It displays, collects, validates, and returns values with a valuechange event.
  5. Attach the type to the action input (the action's Input Rendering).
  6. Pass the values into the existing Flow. Test and check the real Contact.

The architecture lesson: UI collects, agent orchestrates, Flow performs.

11

Booking approval process

Where this comes from Approval task · p.226

New booking requests need staff approval before they become Confirmed.

  1. Create an approval process on Trip_Booking__c.
  2. Submit eligible In Process bookings. Assign to travel staff.
  3. On approval: set status to Confirmed. Keep Booked Seats unchanged.
  4. On rejection: set status to Cancelled (exact picklist value). Release the seats from the departure. Set Seats Released to true.
  5. Check Seats Released before subtracting. Never release twice.
  6. Make sure approve or reject cannot repeat in a way that corrupts counts.
  7. Verify the validation rule that keeps Booked Seats between zero and Total Seats.

Caution CreateBooking currently makes the booking In Process. Approval submission must be configured separately. An approval process does not release seats by itself. I add a record-triggered Flow or Apex for rejection, guarded against double release. I do not release seats on approval. I create no Case or custom escalation record.

The note also says the two fields live on different records: Booked_Seats__c on the departure and Seats_Released__c on the booking. So the rejection automation updates both records. (One line in the notes about a single Update Records element is mixed-language and unclear. I do not rely on it.)

Tests: eligible booking can be submitted. Approval gives Confirmed with no seat change. Rejection gives Cancelled and releases once. A second release is blocked. A failure leaves no inconsistent status or seat count. I do not call it complete until both approval and rejection are tested. Status unknown: the notes do not record the test results.

12

Identity and security

Where this comes from Architecture §6 · p.28 · Security notes · p.224

Searching by email and creating a Contact does not prove the visitor owns that email. Someone could type another person's email and try to read or change that person's bookings.

Concept Question it answers
Contact resolution Which Contact matches the email?
Identity verification What proves this visitor controls or may use that identity?
Authorisation Which booking records may this verified visitor read or change?

I keep these three apart. For a public booking site, I do not expose booking management just because someone knows an email. I look for an authenticated customer or verified messaging identity supported by my channel.

Prescribed Controls:

  • Guests see only approved destination and package data.
  • Guests cannot query arbitrary Contacts or bookings.
  • Enforce record access and field-level permissions for actions that run as the agent user.
  • Never show Contact IDs to the traveler. Every action re-checks ownership server-side.
  • Protect Contact creation from spam, enumeration and duplicates (duplicate rule, email format check, rate limits, monitoring; CAPTCHA or login in production).
  • Handle duplicate email and concurrent Contact creation explicitly.
  • The agent user and its permissions are part of the security design, not a last step.

Caution In the current build, email identifies a Contact. It is not authentication. This is fine for a demo of browsing and booking. For booking management the notes want email plus booking number. The production answers are an authenticated Experience Cloud login or OTP (optional scope). The final Agent Script tells the agent not to treat email lookup as proof of identity and not to send OTP codes.

Optional Improvements I can add after the required scope: OTP email verification (last, to avoid the email limit), authenticated login, CAPTCHA.

Before I build, I check what the org really has. The notes say a base Developer Edition org does not automatically give Enhanced Chat v2 availability, and that Data Cloud (now Data 360) is a prerequisite for the Data Library flow. They say I must not assume everything is available together because a feature appears in Setup.

Check Why it matters When

Service Cloud and Omni-Channel Queue-based support and routing First prerequisite

I verify the exact supported mix of: agent type, Experience Cloud site, Enhanced Chat v2 deployment, human escalation and Custom Lightning Type. The Enhanced Chat agent guide lists the prerequisites.

Reference build My org: a new Agentforce and Data Cloud Developer Edition org. I checked that Agentforce, Agentforce Studio and Data Cloud are present. Then I enabled Einstein Generative AI, Agentforce and Prompt Builder, and created two Admin users (Admin A and B).

  • Developer Edition orgs may be ended after 45 days of inactivity. I log in weekly and keep the repo current.
  • Data Cloud was renamed Data 360 in October 2025. Setup may show either name.
  • Sign-up can be flaky. If an error appears, I retry later or from the other link before I change anything.

Recommended agent direction: a customer-facing Agentforce Service Agent on a supported messaging channel, built in Agentforce Builder with Agent Script if my org has it. Why: it separates conversation from business operations, each subagent has a narrow purpose, and Agent Script gives explicit conditions where I do not want to rely only on the LLM.

Team and Git workflow

Where this comes from Architecture §9–11 · p.33–40 · M0 · p.192

One GitHub repo, two laptops, one integration org. The repo is the shared source. The org is where things run.

Concept Meaning
GitHub collaboration Share source, review changes, keep history
Metadata deployment Move supported metadata between source and org
Shared org collaboration Same live org, so edits can overwrite each other
Environment promotion Move tested changes to a later environment through a controlled deploy

GitHub does not auto-sync a live agent. It can version and deploy supported agent metadata. The notes cite agent metadata changes in API v68 and an Agentforce DX flow for retrieving and deploying agent definitions. See Move an Agent to a New Org (the page title comes from my notes; I did not re-fetch it).

I read this as short feature branches that always return to main through a reviewed pull request.

Collaboration rules

  1. Each person logs in to the org with their own Salesforce CLI session. Never share passwords, tokens or auth files.
  2. One feature branch per person. Names like feature/data-model, feature/booking-apex, feature/agent-config, feature/experience-site.
  3. Narrow pull requests, reviewed before merge.
  4. One deployment owner for the integration org. One person deploys a shared component at a time.
  5. Retrieve or commit existing changes before touching a shared component.
  6. Test in the org after merge. A clean Git merge is not a successful deploy.
  7. Keep credentials, local-only files and secrets out of Git.
  8. Never let both people edit the same live agent or shared Flow at once.

Repository layout: force-app/main/default/ with objects, classes, flows, lwc, permissionsets, prompts, lightningTypes; plus manifest/package.xml, scripts/sample-data/, docs/ (architecture, data-model, security, testing, deployment), .gitignore, README.md.

Shell
sf org login web --alias wanderway --set-default
sf org display --target-org wanderway
sf project generate --name wanderway --template standard

git switch main && git pull
git switch -c feature/a-seat-engine
sf project deploy start --target-org wanderway
sf project retrieve start --target-org wanderway   # after any Setup UI change
git add -p && git commit -m "feat: ..."
git push -u origin feature/a-seat-engine           # open PR, other person reviews

sf project deploy start --target-org wanderway --dry-run   # validate first
sf apex run test --test-level RunLocalTests --wait 10 --target-org wanderway

Add .sfdx/, .sf/, node_modules/, *.key, *.crt, .env, auth*.txt, *.log to .gitignore. Protect main: require a PR and one approval. For conflicts: git pull --rebase origin main, fix files, git add, git rebase --continue. For rollback, revert the commit and redeploy. Do not delete fields that hold data. Run the seed script only in a fresh org.

Contracts I agree on before splitting work: object and field API names, Apex action inputs and outputs, Flow variable names and types, agent action names and descriptions, booking status values and transitions, traveler verification results, error response style, permissions, test data and acceptance criteria.

Roadmap and milestones

Where this comes from Architecture §11 · p.37 · Build guide M0–M10 · p.192–224

Order matters. Booking actions before the departure model would cause rework. I finish and verify each milestone first.

I read this as a spine with two side branches (flows and the policy library) that join at the agent.

Milestones and their acceptance tests (architecture plan)
Milestone Owner Acceptance
0 Architecture and org readiness Both I can show the architecture is supported and the org capabilities exist
1 Data foundation A Records and relationships work. Unauthorised users cannot read protected data

Mandatory: all four objects, seat rules, secure booking access, primary agent with three subagents, Flows and Apex actions, policy grounding, site pages and LWCs, Custom Lightning Type, human escalation, GitHub collaboration, comprehensive tests.

Build guide M0 to M10 in one line each

The seed data in the guide: 5 destinations (Goa, Kerala, Ladakh, Jaipur, Andaman) and 10 packages across Family, Luxury, Honeymoon, Budget and Adventure types. One package is inactive on purpose. Each package gets 3 departures. The first is sold out. The second has 2 seats left for a last-seat test. The third is inactive. These are test fixtures, and the notes mark the example URLs as example.com.

Agent-level instructions (reference)

You are the WanderWay Travel Planner. Help travelers explore destinations, compare packages, check availability, book trips, manage bookings, and answer travel policy questions. Never state a price, seat count, availability, or booking status unless an action returned it. Never reveal internal IDs. Always get an explicit "yes" before creating, changing, or cancelling a booking. Report action failures honestly. Politely decline unrelated requests. Offer or perform human escalation when the traveler asks for a human, has an unresolved issue, is very upset, has a payment or billing dispute, reports a missed or cancelled trip or an emergency during a trip, or when an action fails twice.

Subagent rules in short:

  • Trip Planning: collect, then search. Recommend only from results. Need package, date (with year) and travelers before checking. Use the availability result as the only source of seats and price. Offer only returned alternatives. Verify by email (ask name only if new). Show the summary. Ask for explicit confirmation. Then create the booking with the stored reference. Report the real booking number and status. If it fails, say so plainly. Do not retry automatically.
  • Booking Management: verify first. Use only the stored reference. Confirm before cancel or change. If a change fails, say the original booking is unchanged. Do not state refund amounts. Support handles refunds.
  • Travel Information: answer only from approved material. If not covered, say so and offer help. Never mention files or links. Redirect live price or availability questions to planning.

Foundations I studied

Where this comes from Data 360 · p.289–320 · Agentforce · p.321–333 · Agent Script · p.334–343

These notes sit under the project. They explain why the design looks the way it does. Added context pieces are marked.

Data 360

Data 360 connects data, prepares it, models it, unifies it, helps me understand it and lets me act on it. It is a data foundation, not just a customer database.

I read this as a pipeline. Different systems store the same person in different ways. Model it, then use Identity Resolution to decide which records are the same person.

  • Model vs identity: the data model asks how should data be organised? Identity Resolution asks which records belong to the same person?
  • A unified profile is not a "golden record" that overwrites sources. It is more like a key ring linking records of one person.
  • Developer docs describe the path as data source → DLO → DMO → Identity Resolution → Unified DMO (Data Lake Object, Data Model Object).
  • Calculated Insights make metrics such as lifetime value. Data Actions send events to targets such as Flow.
  • Agentforce link: Data 360 supports structured and unstructured data (documents, emails, chat logs) that an agent can use as context. Ethical use: be clear about value, collect only what I need, protect sensitive data. More data means more context and more responsibility.

Agentforce basics

Term Simplest meaning
Agent AI system that can understand, reason and act
Topic (now subagent) Area of work
Instructions Rules and guidance for behaviour
Action Something the agent can do (Flow, Apex, prompt)
Data Information the agent can use
Grounding Linking answers to trusted information
Guardrails Boundaries for safe behaviour
Permissions What the agent or user may access or do

I read this as understanding first, then reasoning over data and actions. Around it: security, guardrails, testing, monitoring. Flow is a predefined process I define. Agentforce takes free language and chooses capabilities. They work together: the agent calls an action, the action runs a Flow.

When an agent misbehaves I ask: what did I expect, what happened, where did it go wrong (topic, instructions, action, data, permission, guardrail), fix, test again. An action that exists but will not run may be a permission problem on the running user.

Agent Script

Agent Script mixes flexible LLM reasoning with deterministic logic. The LLM is probabilistic, but some steps must always happen, such as verification before showing order details. Agent Script also does context engineering: it rebuilds the prompt each turn from variables and state so the LLM sees only what matters now.

Syntax Meaning
key: value Configuration
indentation Structure
@ Reference a resource
# Comment
-> Execute logic
\| Text sent to the LLM
{! } Insert a dynamic value
... Let the LLM fill an action input
if Condition

Building blocks, top to bottom: config (who is the agent), variables (memory, mutable or linked), system (global behaviour, welcome and error messages), start_agent (every message starts here), topics/subagents (areas with their own actions and instructions), actions (what the agent can do), reasoning (links instructions and actions to execution). The Agent Script reference describes the blocks.

Two ways to call an action: run (code decides, must happen) and LLM tool (the LLM decides when to use it). In my router, before_reasoning is the code path. The transition to actions are tools the LLM picks.

NOT, || OR, && AND, ; end of statement, { } block, ( ) parameters, 'text' literal, @InvocableVariable exposes a field as an input or output, @InvocableMethod exposes a method to automation including Agentforce, with sharing applies record-sharing rules.

Accuracy and version notes

Where this comes from Collected while I studied. Nothing here changes the notes silently.

  1. API names disagree. Phase 1 and the build guide use different names for four fields (section 3). Action names also differ between the M3 reference classes and the final agent (CheckAvailabilityAction with package code vs CheckAvailabilityAndPrice with package ID).
  2. Validation formula. The cross-object reference may need __r. I verify in the org.
  3. Departure window. 90 days in Phase 2, 3 to 6 months in the brief.
  4. Refund tiers. Placeholder values vs a "do not invent" rule.
  5. Cancel and change scope. The brief implies any active booking. The final Apex only handles In Process with seats not released.
  6. SeatService. Referenced and tested, but its source is missing from my notes.
  7. Escalation template. Offers to log a support case. The brief forbids creating a Case.
  8. Queue name. "Travel Support" in the brief. One note says "Sales Support Queue".
  9. Check Availability review. The earliest-date SOQL filter and missing alternatives on invalid limit or price.
  10. Identity. Email alone identifies a Contact. It does not authenticate. outVerified does not mean ownership.
  11. Terminology. "Topics" are now "subagents". Data Cloud is now "Data 360". UI labels in my notes may have moved. The notes mark many Setup names as VERIFY.
  12. Unclear notes. A short mixed-language note about Update Records, and a few untitled screenshot sections (OWD, Experience site page 2). I do not use them as facts.
  13. Status not stated for: the approval process results, the booking Custom Lightning Type render, the final policy PDF text and the full test run.

Glossary and revision prompts

Term Meaning
Departure One record per package per date. Holds seats
Available Seats Formula: Total Seats − Booked Seats
In Process New booking. Seats held. Awaiting staff review
Seats Released Checkbox that stops seats being released twice
Subagent An agent area of work (formerly topic)
Grounding Basing a reply on trusted records or documents
Idempotent Safe to run twice with the same result
Savepoint A database marker I can roll back to
Omni-Channel Salesforce routing of work to available agents
Custom Lightning Type A schema and UI that tells the agent how to show or collect structured data
Q1. Why can the agent not answer seat counts from the policy PDF?

The Package_Departure__c record is the single source of truth. The PDF holds rules only. The agent must call the availability action.

Q2. Why does Create Booking check seats again?

Availability is a snapshot. Another traveler may book before this one confirms. Create Booking locks the departure, rechecks and reserves in one transaction.

Q3. When do seats get released, and how do I stop a double release?

On reject or cancel. Never on approve. Seats Released flips in the same update that subtracts the seats, and the departure rows are locked.

Q4. Why use a daily scheduled job for Trip Started and Completed?

Triggers and record-triggered flows fire only when a record changes. Dates arriving change nothing.

Q5. What are contact resolution, identity verification and authorisation?

Resolution finds the Contact. Verification proves the visitor owns that identity. Authorisation decides which bookings they may see or change.

Q6. What does the AI decide, and what must Salesforce decide?

The AI understands language and explains. Salesforce decides status, dates, seats, price, ownership, transitions, and whether a transaction or handoff succeeded.

Q7. What does `BookingFlowActive` do?

It makes the router send every message to Trip Planning and Booking until the flow ends, so short replies stay in context.

Built as a revision page. Salesforce UI labels and product names change often, so I check the current documentation and my own org before relying on any step. Items marked Verify are checks my notes ask me to do.
